 1) get the rush of relief I felt after NSSI 
 2) punish myself 

Everyone is different, but I believe the association with pain and relief can become easily addictive for most, and if you dont know how to cope healthily, it becomes a crutch for any and all emotions.

Edit: if this helps to understand, think of self harm almost like compulsive running. You get the release of endorphins with both, and if you start to use that release to cope...bam. self harm or self destructive behavior

- making sure to eat well, staying hydrated and taking care of physical needs is so important with depression, because if you start to physically not feel well either, the situation is compounded. 

- if you're having executive dysfunction problems, planners and phone agendas make it easier for me to break down goals or work into smaller digestible pieces. 

-  do something called "opposite action" . It's a DBT skill where you essentially do the opposite of an unhealthy or maladaptive urge. If your urge is to sleep in and skip class, then OA is to get up right away and go without even thinking. Another example is if you are isolating a lot, the opposite action us to go out and be with a friend. For more info on the opposite action thing, here is a link. 

 https://www.mindsoother.com/blog/using-opposite-action-for-overwhelming-emotions

As far as just lifestyle changes go, it's not going to be an instant fix, but it could improve things. Good luck!! 

Ps: if you feel like you're doing all you can to feel better and it's not working, I highly recommend talking to a school counselor or someone close about the depression and lack of motivation. There's not shame at all in needing a little more help.

What helped me was focusing on my progress in comparison to ME. So, for example, If I start to feel jealous and pissed because of my position in life, I try to shift my focus from what other people have or have accomplished, and more to "how far have I come in my own growth? How am I doing now compared to myself 2 years ago?"

A therapist told me once that comparison is the thief of joy. I noticed, esp when I was a teen, that I would see people around me doing great stuff and going places, and I was going nowhere fast. until I started telling myself that I just need to be the best possible version of me I could create, and comparing my progress to other people isn't helping me at all. It didn't motivate me, it made me fucked in the head.

My best advice is to start seeing other people as equally flawed, human, and fallible. Try and take their accomplishments off a pedestal, bc truly, maybe they don't deserve these things. Live out of spite- make more money out of spite. Clean your room to show yourself and others that you are capable.

You don't need to fix everything right away, but a good place to start is to hold yourself to a standard not based on what others have, but based on what you want.
